> 革。己日乃孚，元亨，利貞，悔亡。

Hexagram 49 is about change, and its character means a hide with the hair scraped off.

## 革: the original sense is "remove the old"

說文: 革，獸皮治去其毛 — an animal hide, processed until the hair is gone.

And this is the most important thing about the character: its original sense already is 去故 — removing what was.

A raw hide becomes usable leather by scraping the hair off, paring the flesh away, working the fat out. What remains is the tough layer.

So 革's sense of "change" is not a metaphor. It is the original sense extended: treat the hide, remove the useless, keep the usable.

Change is never smashing the old. It is processing the old until it can be used.

And there is a beautiful detail: 初九 鞏用黃牛之革 uses 革 in its original sense — leather — not in the hexagram's sense of change.

Nowhere else in the book is a hexagram's name and a line's text the same character used once at origin and once at extension, so clearly. It is as much as saying: the doctrine of change is hidden in the craft of leather.

## 己日

己 is the sixth of the ten stems. Three readings exist (a day in the cycle; 已, "already"; a miswriting of 巳).

This book keeps the sense of "the day the time is ripe," and does not fix it to a date.

## 鞏

鞏: to make firm. 說文 鞏，以韋束也 — to bind something with cured hide.

So 鞏用黃牛之革 is a very concrete sentence: bind it tight with yellow ox hide.

黃牛: yellow is the colour of the centre, the ox a yielding animal. Central and supple — which is the correct way to make a thing firm: not by propping it up rigidly, but by binding it with something that flexes.

## 三就

就: to complete. 革言三就 — the plan of change completed three times over.

三 is "many," not exactly three. Which is the hexagram's discipline against sudden reform: the proposal has to be finished, and finished again.

## 虎變 / 豹變 / 革面

變 here means changing coat, changing markings.

A tiger changing its coat changes the whole pattern at once — the entire bearing comes out new.
A leopard changes its spots: fine, dense, brought out gradually.

革面 is usually read as a criticism (outward compliance, inward refusal). And the 象 says 小人革面，順以從君也 — compliance itself is not the crime; the failure is that it stops at the face.

## 治曆明時

The 象: 君子以治曆明時.

曆 is the calendar; 明時 is to make the seasons legible.

Not "read the situation." This is the actual work: fix the calendar, correct the first month, settle the seasons.

Which is the chapter's idea of change in its most literal form: the thing that must be reformed first is the way time is counted.

## The test

Take a change you are pushing — in an organisation, in yourself. Ask what the hide is: what has to be scraped off, what has to be pared, and what is the tough layer that should remain. 革 does not ask you to destroy the material. It asks whether you know which part is the leather.
